goal: Find the cancellation age window for subscriber winback messages.
whyThisDefault: The age window preserves the established outreach timing after cancellation. The platform keeps its neutral default of requiring retention consent at the send gate.

frozenOn: Existing winback delivery receipts retain their deduplication identity.

runtime.reason: Discovery documents the age window and send gate. The full policy and episode changes need separate qualification.

change.operation: No settings write operation is available for this key.

goal: Set how many minutes a subscription edit quote remains valid before expiry (subscription edit quote TTL, quote expiry, preview validity window).
whyThisDefault: Fifteen minutes preserves the historical quote expiry window across SQL preview functions (customer_subscription_preview_bundle_as_actor and subscription_command_preview) and TypeScript subscription editors (PackageEditorOptions and SizedEditorOptions).

effect.appliesTo: Subsequent uncached SQL edit quote creations in customer_subscription_preview_bundle_as_actor and subscription_command_preview read key='subscription_edit_quote_ttl_minutes' from public.commerce_settings via subscription_edit_quote_ttl_minutes_read(), computing expires_at = previewTime + make_interval(mins => ttlMinutes) consistently in both quote_hash and subscription_edit_quotes. TypeScript editors created via createPostgresPackageEditor and createPostgresSizedEditor accept optional quoteTtlMinutes (1..1440, default 15). When no row exists in public.commerce_settings, the SQL reader defaults to 15 minutes; malformed rows refuse fail-closed with SQLSTATE 22023 subscription_edit_quote_ttl_minutes_policy_invalid without persisting a refusal receipt.
frozenOn: Already persisted subscription_edit_quotes rows and completed preview command receipts (including idempotent replays) retain their recorded quoteHash and expires_at timestamps.

runtime.reason: Install or update the public.commerce_settings row through installSubscriptionEditQuoteTtlMinutesPolicy or supply quoteTtlMinutes on PackageEditorOptions / SizedEditorOptions; runtime SQL edits require a write-capable host connection.

rules.description: Supply exactly revision and ttlMinutes. Revision must be a nonblank string and ttlMinutes an integer from 1 through 1440.

goal: Set the minimum base unit count required when editing a classic subscription (minimum base units, subscription edit floor, package minimum).

absentMeans.description: Both TypeScript (createPostgresPackageEditReadPort) and SQL subscription edit paths fail closed with subscription_reprice_minimum_base_units_unavailable when no valid positive 32-bit integer is stored in commerce_settings.value_text.

whyThisDefault: The platform provides no implicit floor for classic subscription edits; stores must explicitly install a positive 32-bit integer row in commerce_settings.

effect.appliesTo: Classic subscription edit quotes and SQL applies read the installed minimum base-unit count from commerce_settings.value_text; host edit admission checks for drift against configured offer minimums before admitting edits.
frozenOn: Existing active subscriptions and already completed edit command receipts retain their agreed quantities and prices.

runtime.reason: Install or update the commerce_settings row through your store installation step; host edit admission refuses drift against application configuration.

change.operation: No settings write operation is available for this key.

goal: Set the introductory fixed-cycle and graduation-cycle boundaries for sized subscription editing (intro phase, graduation cycle, starter pack editing).

absentMeans.description: Introductory starter-pack subscriptions fail closed in SQL with subscription_edit_invalid_sized_configuration when no valid JSON row is installed in commerce_settings.value_text. In the starter, owned/subscription-editing.ts holds the code copy while owned/demo-seed.ts installs the matching database copy; keep both aligned.

whyThisDefault: The platform provides no implicit introductory phase cutoff; stores must explicitly install fixedThroughCycle and graduationCycle (positive 32-bit integers with graduationCycle > fixedThroughCycle) in commerce_settings when introductory subscriptions use sized editing.

effect.appliesTo: Sized subscription edit commands for introductory starter-pack subscriptions evaluate fixedThroughCycle and graduationCycle (positive 32-bit integers with graduationCycle > fixedThroughCycle) from the installed commerce_settings row in SQL alongside the configured SizedEditPolicy in TypeScript (in the starter, keep owned/subscription-editing.ts aligned with the database row seeded by owned/demo-seed.ts).
frozenOn: Already completed edit command receipts and past paid cycles retain their recorded state.

runtime.reason: Install or update the commerce_settings row together with the application's SizedEditPolicy configuration.

change.operation: No settings write operation is available for this key.

goal: Customize renewal execution input, failure classification, and post-renewal or exhaustion outcome handling (after renewal, renewal policy, dunning exhaustion, failure classification).
whyThisDefault: The platform supplies neutral failure-key defaults via createDefaultRenewalFailurePolicy and leaves post-exhaustion actions unconfigured so hosts compose AutomaticRenewalPolicy, RenewalOutcomePolicy, and RenewalFailurePolicy from @openlup/platform/subscriptions explicitly.

effect.appliesTo: Subsequent renewal runs and failure-handling passes invoke the bound AutomaticRenewalPolicy, RenewalOutcomePolicy, and RenewalFailurePolicy callbacks from @openlup/platform/subscriptions.
frozenOn: Already recorded renewal operations, retry obligations, dunning cases, and completed command receipts retain their persisted state.

runtime.reason: The policy hooks are executable server code implementing AutomaticRenewalPolicy, RenewalOutcomePolicy, and RenewalFailurePolicy from @openlup/platform/subscriptions.

runtime.reason: Native cadence is expressed in days.

goal: Offer custom subscription pause durations.

runtime.reason: Native lifecycle commands support two weeks, one month and indefinite.

goal: Require delivery evidence and move alignment only later.

runtime.reason: A late delivery extends the cycle without stacking deliveries. A replacement counts only after arrival.

goal: Admit or refuse proposed subscription lines, quantities, and cadences before pricing a subscription edit (edit terms admission, offer admission, cadence validation).
whyThisDefault: Omitting admitSubscriptionTerms (SubscriptionTermsAdmission from @openlup/platform/subscriptions) preserves native subscription editing behavior with no application-specific offer filter beyond platform minimums and representation bounds.

effect.appliesTo: Fresh subscription edit previews and applies invoke the bound SubscriptionTermsAdmission callback (admitSubscriptionTerms from @openlup/platform/subscriptions) after normalization and before pricing or quote persistence.
frozenOn: Active subscription terms and already completed matching command receipts replay without re-evaluating changed admission rules.

runtime.reason: The callback is executable server code implementing SubscriptionTermsAdmission from @openlup/platform/subscriptions.

goal: Schedule introductory discounts by renewal cycle.

goal: Admit or refuse fresh customer subscription lifecycle commands such as skip, slide, pause, resume, cancel, order_now, and reactivate (command admission, pause presets, account actions).
whyThisDefault: Omitting admitSubscriptionCommand on NativeSubscriptionCommandBinding from @openlup/platform/subscriptions (typed as SubscriptionCommandAdmission from @openlup/platform/subscriptions/contracts) preserves native command behavior across all supported lifecycle actions subject to platform state and payment fences.

effect.appliesTo: Fresh subscription lifecycle previews and commands invoke the bound admitSubscriptionCommand callback on NativeSubscriptionCommandBinding from @openlup/platform/subscriptions (implementing SubscriptionCommandAdmission from @openlup/platform/subscriptions/contracts) after replay checks and before durable writes.
frozenOn: Completed command receipts and existing pauses or cycle dates replay and retain their stored outcomes.

runtime.reason: The callback is executable server code implementing SubscriptionCommandAdmission from @openlup/platform/subscriptions/contracts via admitSubscriptionCommand on NativeSubscriptionCommandBinding from @openlup/platform/subscriptions.

goal: Calculate subscription reschedule calendar-day boundaries in a configured IANA time zone (reschedule time zone, slide calendar day, market timezone).
whyThisDefault: UTC preserves historical epoch-day and UTC calendar-day reschedule comparisons across subscription_apply_lifecycle_action, subscription_command_preview, subscription_command_apply, customer_support_apply_subscription_action_v1, and save-offer reschedule target calculation.

effect.appliesTo: Subsequent fresh slide_next_cycle evaluations in subscription_apply_lifecycle_action, subscription_command_preview, subscription_command_apply, customer_support_apply_subscription_action_v1, and reschedule save-offer target calculation in Postgres command stores read key='subscription_reschedule_timezone' from public.commerce_settings via subscription_reschedule_timezone_read(). When no row exists in public.commerce_settings, the SQL reader defaults to 'UTC'; malformed or unrecognized IANA time zone rows refuse fail-closed with SQLSTATE 22023 subscription_reschedule_timezone_policy_invalid.
frozenOn: Completed subscription_command_receipts, customer_support_subscription_commands, and already scheduled subscription next_cycle_at timestamps retain their recorded values.

runtime.reason: Install or update the public.commerce_settings row through installSubscriptionRescheduleTimeZonePolicy or your store deployment step; runtime edits require a write-capable host connection.

rules.description: The policy must be a JSON object with only revision (nonblank string) and timeZone (valid IANA time zone name recognized by PostgreSQL pg_timezone_names).

goal: Set the 3-rung retry backoff schedule in hours for subscription payment failures (subscription retry schedule, renewal retry policy, dunning schedule, backoff hours).
whyThisDefault: Twenty-four, 72, and 168 hours preserve the historical 3-rung retry cadence (retries on days 1, 4, and 11 after the initial decline) across both 3-argument subscription_retry_apply_failure and provider-recorded failures applied through payment_provider_result_apply without explicit p_cadence.

effect.appliesTo: Subsequent failure recordings via 3-argument subscription_retry_apply_failure and provider-recorded renewal failures via payment_provider_result_apply when p_cadence is omitted or NULL read key='subscription_retry_schedule' from public.commerce_settings via subscription_retry_schedule_read(). Explicit p_cadence passed to 4-argument subscription_retry_apply_failure or 12-argument payment_provider_result_apply takes precedence. When no row exists in public.commerce_settings, the SQL reader defaults to [24, 72, 168]; malformed rows refuse fail-closed with SQLSTATE 22023 subscription_retry_schedule_policy_invalid.
frozenOn: Already recorded subscription_retry_obligations next_retry_at schedules, completed subscription_retry_receipts (including idempotent replays), and already opened subscription_dunning_cases keep their recorded retry timestamps.

runtime.reason: Install or update the public.commerce_settings row through installSubscriptionRetrySchedulePolicy or your store deployment step; runtime edits require a write-capable host connection.

rules.description: Supply exactly revision and backoffHours. Revision must be a nonblank string and backoffHours an array of exactly three integers from 1 through 2147483647.

whyThisDefault: The platform provides no default demand-to-quantity sizing formula; hosts supply SizedHostPorts.proposePortion from @openlup/platform/subscriptions, or refuse demand-driven resizing when unconfigured.

runtime.reason: The callback is executable server code implementing SizedHostPorts.proposePortion from @openlup/platform/subscriptions.
